documentary.title: The Black Death: How 12 Ships Brought the Plague to Europe

shorts.title: The Ships of Death
shorts.hook: Twelve ships sailed into a harbor in Sicily. Almost everyone on board was dead.

shorts.title: Were the Rats Innocent?
shorts.hook: For centuries, rats took the blame. Some scientists now think people and their fleas spread it faster.

shorts.title: Named After a Symptom
shorts.hook: Bubonic plague is named after one horrifying symptom.

shorts.title: The Plague Doctor Myth
shorts.hook: The famous beaked plague mask didn’t exist during the Black Death. It showed up about 300 years later.

shorts.title: One in Three
shorts.hook: Think of every third person you know. Now imagine them gone.

shorts.title: Florence Lost Half
shorts.hook: Florence may have lost half its people in a single year.

shorts.title: The Siege of Caffa
shorts.hook: In 1346, an army hurled dead bodies over a city wall.

shorts.title: A Book Born From the Plague
shorts.hook: One of Europe’s most famous books is about ten people hiding from the Black Death.

shorts.title: The Pope Between Two Fires
shorts.hook: The Pope waited out the plague sitting between two huge fires.

shorts.title: Ring Around the Rosie
shorts.hook: You’ve heard this nursery rhyme is about the plague. There’s no evidence it is.

shorts.title: Blamed on Bad Air
shorts.hook: Doctors were sure the plague spread through bad air.

shorts.title: London’s Plague Pits
shorts.hook: London dug long trenches for the dead.

shorts.title: The Flagellants
shorts.hook: Thousands of people marched across Europe whipping themselves bloody, believing it would stop the plague.

shorts.title: Looking for Someone to Blame
shorts.hook: When people couldn’t explain the plague, they turned on their neighbors.

shorts.title: The Island That Escaped
shorts.hook: One corner of Europe escaped the Black Death, for about fifty years.

shorts.title: Quarantine Was Born Here
shorts.hook: The word quarantine comes from the Italian for forty days.

shorts.title: It Still Exists
shorts.hook: The bacterium behind the Black Death still infects people today.

shorts.title: Dancing Skeletons
shorts.hook: After the plague, European art filled up with dancing skeletons.

shorts.title: The Plague Made Workers Rich
shorts.hook: After the Black Death, peasants suddenly had something new: bargaining power.

shorts.title: It Kept Coming Back
shorts.hook: The Black Death wasn’t the end. Plague kept returning for 300 years.

shorts.title: Written in Your DNA
shorts.hook: The Black Death may still be written in your DNA.

documentary.title: Pompeii: The Last 24 Hours of a Roman City

shorts.title: The Plaster Bodies
shorts.hook: The bodies of Pompeii aren’t bodies. They’re hollows in the ash, filled with plaster.

shorts.title: Not Just Pompeii
shorts.hook: Vesuvius didn’t bury one city. It buried several.

shorts.title: Vesuvius Erupted in 1944
shorts.hook: The volcano that buried Pompeii erupted again in 1944.

shorts.title: We Had the Date Wrong
shorts.hook: For centuries we had the date of Pompeii’s destruction wrong.

shorts.title: The Dog of Pompeii
shorts.hook: One of Pompeii’s most haunting casts isn’t a person.

shorts.title: The Eyewitness
shorts.hook: We know what Vesuvius looked like because a teenager wrote it down.

shorts.title: Pliny Sailed Toward It
shorts.hook: When Vesuvius erupted, one Roman admiral sailed straight toward it.

shorts.title: The Earthquake Warning
shorts.hook: Seventeen years before the eruption, Pompeii got a warning.

shorts.title: Roman Election Posters
shorts.hook: Pompeii’s walls are covered in 2,000-year-old campaign ads.

shorts.title: Roman Fast Food
shorts.hook: Romans grabbed fast food too, and archaeologists found the counter.

shorts.title: The Garden of the Fugitives
shorts.hook: Thirteen people were running for the gate. They didn’t make it.

shorts.title: Dug Through by Accident
shorts.hook: In the 1590s, workers dug right through Pompeii and didn’t realize it.

shorts.title: 81 Loaves in the Oven
shorts.hook: In one Pompeii bakery, archaeologists found 81 loaves still in the oven.

shorts.title: Roman Crosswalks
shorts.hook: Pompeii’s streets had stepping stones, and they tell us something about the traffic.

shorts.title: Most People Escaped
shorts.hook: Most of Pompeii’s people probably got out.

shorts.title: The Walls Talk
shorts.hook: Pompeii’s walls are covered in 2,000-year-old graffiti. Some of it is very rude.

shorts.title: The Villa of the Mysteries
shorts.hook: One house in Pompeii holds paintings no one has fully explained.

shorts.title: Still Buried
shorts.hook: Around a third of Pompeii still hasn’t been dug up.

shorts.title: Herculaneum’s Last Seconds
shorts.hook: In the town next door, it was over in moments.

shorts.title: Scrolls Read by AI
shorts.hook: Scrolls burned by Vesuvius are being read for the first time, with help from AI.

shorts.title: It Rained Stones
shorts.hook: For hours before the deadly part began, it rained stones on Pompeii.

documentary.title: The Fall of Constantinople: The Last Day of the Roman Empire
chapters: A City of a Thousand Years

shorts.title: The Cannon Nobody Bought
shorts.hook: The engineer offered his giant cannon to the Byzantines first. They couldn’t afford it.

shorts.title: The Walls That Held 1,000 Years
shorts.hook: These walls kept out almost every army for a thousand years.

shorts.title: Greek Fire
shorts.hook: The Byzantines had a weapon that burned on water, and the recipe is lost.

shorts.title: Ships Over a Hill
shorts.hook: A chain blocked the sultan’s navy, so he moved his ships over land.

shorts.title: Hagia Sophia
shorts.hook: For nearly a thousand years, this was the biggest cathedral in the world.

shorts.title: The Last Service
shorts.hook: The night before the city fell, Christians gathered in Hagia Sophia one last time.

shorts.title: The Sultan Was 21
shorts.hook: The man who ended the Roman Empire was 21 years old.

shorts.title: The Commander Who Fell
shorts.hook: When one wounded commander left the walls, the defense collapsed.

shorts.title: 53 Days
shorts.hook: The siege of Constantinople lasted 53 days.

shorts.title: The Gate Left Open
shorts.hook: One story says the city fell because someone left a small gate open.

shorts.title: Outnumbered
shorts.hook: The defenders were outnumbered by as much as ten to one.

shorts.title: The Chain
shorts.hook: A giant chain across the harbor kept the Ottoman navy out.

shorts.title: The Emperor Who Vanished
shorts.hook: The last Roman emperor charged into battle and was never seen again.

shorts.title: Sacked by Crusaders First
shorts.hook: Constantinople had already been sacked once, by Christian crusaders.

shorts.title: Where ‘Istanbul’ Comes From
shorts.hook: The name Istanbul likely comes from a Greek phrase meaning ‘to the city.’

shorts.title: Rome Lasted Until 1453
shorts.hook: The Roman Empire didn’t end in 476. Half of it lasted almost another thousand years.

shorts.title: Caesar of Rome
shorts.hook: After the conquest, the sultan called himself Caesar of Rome.

shorts.title: The Dark Moon
shorts.hook: Days before the final attack, an eclipse darkened the moon.

shorts.title: The Day the Middle Ages Ended
shorts.hook: Many historians mark the end of the Middle Ages with one day in 1453.

shorts.title: Scholars Fled West
shorts.hook: Greek scholars fled to Italy, carrying ancient books with them.

shorts.title: They Called Themselves Romans
shorts.hook: The Byzantines never called themselves Byzantines.

documentary.title: The Salem Witch Trials: How a Town Turned on Itself

shorts.title: Nobody Was Burned
shorts.hook: No one was burned at the stake in Salem.

shorts.title: Tituba
shorts.hook: The first people accused in Salem included an enslaved woman named Tituba.

shorts.title: Confess and Live
shorts.hook: In Salem, confessing could save your life.

shorts.title: It Started With Two Girls
shorts.hook: In January 1692, two girls in a minister’s house began having fits.

shorts.title: The Youngest Accused
shorts.hook: A girl of four or five was jailed as a witch.

shorts.title: Over 200 Accused
shorts.hook: More than 200 people were accused in Salem.

shorts.title: More Weight
shorts.hook: Giles Corey was crushed under stones for two days. Legend says he only asked for more weight.

shorts.title: Where the Gallows Stood
shorts.hook: The exact spot of Salem’s hangings was only confirmed in 2016.

shorts.title: The Minister on Horseback
shorts.hook: A minister on horseback urged the crowd to go ahead with a hanging.

shorts.title: The Moldy Bread Theory
shorts.hook: Some researchers think Salem’s ‘witchcraft’ may have started with moldy rye.

shorts.title: The Perfect Prayer
shorts.hook: A condemned man recited the Lord’s Prayer perfectly on the gallows.

shorts.title: The Touch Test
shorts.hook: In Salem, a touch could be taken as proof.

shorts.title: Convicted by a Ghost
shorts.hook: In Salem, you could be convicted because someone said your spirit attacked them.

shorts.title: It Reached the Governor
shorts.hook: The panic ended soon after it reached the governor’s own household.

shorts.title: The Witch Cake
shorts.hook: A cake baked with urine was fed to a dog to find a witch.

shorts.title: The Dogs of Salem
shorts.hook: Even two dogs were killed during the Salem panic.

shorts.title: The Jurors Apologized
shorts.hook: Five years later, twelve jurors signed an apology.

shorts.title: The Crucible
shorts.hook: The most famous play about Salem was really about 1950s America.

shorts.title: Cleared in 2022
shorts.hook: The last Salem ‘witch’ wasn’t officially cleared until 2022.

shorts.title: Which Salem?
shorts.hook: The Salem witch trials didn’t start in the town most people picture.

shorts.title: Salem Wasn’t the Worst
shorts.hook: Salem wasn’t Europe’s or America’s worst witch hunt. Not even close.
